status: Validated deeper-review checkpoint, including JAR class selection and PE-hosted .NET bundle extraction. Not a completed review of all 191 previously deferred samples; outstanding work and limitations remain recorded below.
safety: Static parsing, disassembly and data-only unpacking. No specimen executed, remote stage fetched, or dependency installed from a specimen.
feed_policy: Every sample has threat-feed context. Reputation is evidence to investigate, not proof of behavior in the supplied version or hash.

engine_changes.dotnet_bundle: Authorized PE-hosted .NET single-file extraction added in src/analyzers/archive/dotnet_bundle.rs, routed through ArchiveAnalyzer's guarded member windows from PEAnalyzer. Supports versions 1, 2 and 6, including raw-DEFLATE members. Preserves per-member identity/provenance, detects partial extraction and propagates memory limits, cancellation and archive depth. Manifest parsing, candidate count and output allocations are bounded; no assembly is loaded or executed.

Both memory and disk regressions pass, including a detecting class outside the top-20 salience sample; the original Corz JAR retains i.class and its suspicious finding in both modes.

corz.assessment: obscured loader substantially recovered; complete payload and exfiltration flow not yet proven
corz.separate_paths: Readable zr classes implement license/HWID bypass through native memory patches, pinned RNG/time and loopback replay. Separate root classes a through j implement a heavily obscured loader. A crack's memory patches are not used as proof of credential theft.
corz.call_table: Recovered all 1740 XOR-protected owner/member/descriptor records as data. Each had one syntax-valid decoding candidate. Constant and known-bit arithmetic verified 425 dynamic call sites against their decoder-key upper halves, with zero inconsistent bindings. Unknown operands were not guessed. All 168 dynamic calls in f.a()V were bound this way.
corz.verified_calls: f.a()V obtains the current Minecraft session, calls its access-token getter at bytecode offset 641 and username getter at 673, stores the token in local 3, passes that same local to an obscured three-string helper at 1994, constructs a ProcessBuilder at 11744 and calls start on that process builder at 12532. This establishes token access and a helper handoff, not yet a complete token-to-network or token-to-process-argument proof.
corz.native_bootstrap: Parsed the wrapper's indexed s1 resource as data and recovered a 25088-byte x86_64 Windows DLL at offset 25, SHA-256 8fd1f83269f346ea2440e92720dac9517384f697faaf2dec14461b589d4ff56c. Atomscan reports no suspicious/hostile findings on that bootstrap. The separate 22382520-byte encrypted native resource remains unresolved; this is not an acquittal.
corz.coverage: Added a suspicious shifted-XOR/callsite-resolver layout finding. All 14 checks pass: eleven generated class-format controls, both JAR extraction modes with 25 higher-salience decoys, and the actual external resolver class. Names alone, either layout alone, altered XOR/shift/backedge and each missing API marker do not match. No control may produce hostile findings. The original Corz JAR retains i.class in both extraction modes, reports this new suspicious finding on that child and the root, and retains the existing character-store finding. Neither mode reports a hostile trait.
corz.engine_gap: Cleave's prepass called scan_bytes_filtered, which intentionally discards inline-YARA results. Its empty returned vector was then treated as no interesting hit. i.class was skipped by the top-20 selector despite matching in isolation. A synthetic JAR with 25 higher-salience decoys reproduces this miss on the pre-fix CLI.
corz.hygiene_diagnosis: The lossy projection is documented but hidden behind the generic scan_bytes_filtered name and a Vec<YaraMatch> return type. History places the selector call in f952c931 (2026-09-05); the discard behavior predates it. Both extraction modes already share a triage helper, so duplicated algorithms are not the cause. A named result exposing both channels and explicit lossy projections would reduce this API footgun; no broad YARA API rewrite was undertaken.
corz.limits: 1349 root-class dynamic call sites still lack fully verified operand bindings. Encoded runtime strings, the encrypted native resource and complete source-to-sink relationships require further review. No specimen, JVM bootstrap, native library or network stage was executed. No pool disposition applied.

essential.assessment: malicious RAT behavior confirmed by Java and managed IL review
essential.java_flow: The mod's static early hook invokes LoaderBridge, which copies its embedded Realtek-named EXE/PDB into a temporary directory and launches the copied EXE via ProcessBuilder. The same recovered path reaches the process invocation.
essential.bundle: The 107231972-byte native EXE contains a version 6 .NET single-file bundle. Data-only decompression recovered 451 members totaling 240268667 uncompressed bytes, including the 61440-byte application assembly Realtek HD Audio x64.dll.
essential.managed_flow: Reviewed IL implements polling keylogging with buffered character transmission, C2-dispatched cmd.exe shell input/output, file transfer/execution, Run-key and scheduled-task persistence, screen streaming, remote input and hidden-desktop control. Configuration selects a TLS/WebSocket C2 endpoint; no network connection was made.
essential.coverage_gap: The native host has no CLR directory; previous analysis saw the native runtime but did not unpack the compressed application assembly. The standalone assembly originally had no suspicious or hostile traits despite the recovered behavior.
essential.rule_change: Added a neutral ToUnicode observation and a neutral high-bit/byte-limit CIL backedge observation, composed with managed polling and recording markers into one suspicious finding. The available facts do not bind API tokens and recorded characters to a send, so the rule deliberately does not claim hostile source-to-sink proof.
essential.engine_scope: User explicitly authorized .NET bundle extraction in the sibling Cleave repository. PE-hosted bundle versions 1, 2 and 6 now use the existing windowed member-analysis pipeline. The implementation bounds manifest work and expanded output, propagates request limits/cancellation and container depth, preserves member hashes/paths, rejects unsafe paths, keeps duplicate occurrences and reports partial extraction. Installed binaries have not been replaced; ELF/Mach-O host integration is not part of this change.
essential.verified_results: Five bundle unit tests and nine synthetic CLI controls pass. The final native-host and full-JAR regressions both recover the exact application SHA-256, attach the suspicious recording finding to that assembly and roll it up to the root. The native report has 453 file records; the full JAR has 1025. The support-library regression retains neutral observations and has zero suspicious or hostile findings after retiring the unsupported Temp-stager composite. Final reports: /tmp/gauntlet-deep/bundle-regression-final/; runner log: /tmp/gauntlet-deep/bundle-regression-final.log.
essential.native_support_library: Extraction exposed encoded-temp-command-stager on the bundled OpenCvSharpExtern.dll (SHA-256 2817d96183d22161d0d584b46dbebd9806cdd62ab0d8c4148dbcf685404e6f23). It combined Base64-alphabet strings, Temp APIs, cmd.exe and process APIs without binding them to a staged payload. Retired the unsupported composite, retained all four observations. This correction does not attest the library against an upstream release.
